extracted.intended_audience: MER leaders, mathematics education researchers, mathematicians and K-12/math-education practitioners interested in evaluating MER's impact
extracted.subtask_description: Rubric and survey-based criteria used to assess the MER Forum’s effectiveness in fostering communication, individual and systemic change, and departmental/institutional support for mathematics education reform. Focuses on community-building, workshop impact, pedagogical change, and indicators of systemic reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of people brought together / uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: The types of people brought together by the MER Forum is its most unique aspect; MER attracts a different subset of professionals (research-oriented higher education mathematicians) than other organizations and provides a niche for mathematicians who want to be involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments emphasize MER’s uniqueness in reaching university-level instructors and research mathematicians who would not otherwise engage with math-education organizations. Use as an indicator of MER’s reach and distinct role relative to other organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridging mathematicians and mathematics educators
rubrics_metrics.description: MER serves as a bridge between the cultures of research mathematicians and mathematics educators, facilitating dialogue and interaction among mathematicians, mathematics-educators and K-12 teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether MER creates events and contexts where neither side feels like 'outsiders' and whether it brings together a strong mix of research mathematicians with mathematics educators; measure participants' qualitative reports of cross-group dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating communication and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which MER facilitates communication and collaboration between mathematicians and mathematics educators, broadly defined to include familiarity with mathematics education literature, key education issues, and personal collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via survey items (e.g., percent who consult educational literature, consult math-educators for research, frequency of collaboration). Low levels indicate limited cross-community corroboration and risk of 'recreating the wheel.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation of educational research literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether mathematicians usually consult literature in the field of educational research for information about mathematics education reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey item with response categories (Strongly Disagree → Strongly Agree). Used to gauge mathematicians' engagement with published education research; the report notes ~40% agreement among mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consulting mathematics educators for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether participants usually consult mathematics educators for research about mathematics education reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey-measured item; a majority reportedly consult mathematics educators, and this metric is an indicator of cross-disciplinary consultation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of direct collaboration with educators
rubrics_metrics.description: How often respondents formally or informally collaborate with educators in education departments on their own campus (Never → More than 2 times/month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to quantify personal collaboration; document highlights 'once or twice each semester' as a common benchmark and indicates limited corroboration if frequencies are low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of mathematics education issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported increase in awareness of issues in mathematics education reform as a result of MER participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey item (Strongly Disagree → Strongly Agree). The report cites >70% of mathematicians and K-12 educators and >50% of math-educators reporting increased awareness; use as an indicator of individual-level impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Networking and dissemination (access to colleagues)
rubrics_metrics.description: MER’s effectiveness in providing networking opportunities and dissemination channels, giving participants access to people and information they would otherwise not know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative comments and survey items (comfort contacting MER colleagues, frequency of contacts) are evidence. Look for measures like >70% comfortable contacting colleagues and counts of contact frequencies across topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshops as settings for cross-community interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness of MER workshops in attracting mathematics educators and K-12 personnel and facilitating cross-community connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider workshop attendance composition, whether workshops are targeted to both mathematicians and educators, and participants’ suggestions for more sessions explicitly designed for K-12 audiences (breakouts, panels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of K-12 teachers in MER activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether MER explicitly includes K-12 personnel in activities that lend credibility to their experience (e.g., organizing breakout sessions, participating on panels, designing K-12-focused sessions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess representation and role of K-12 teachers in program planning and presentations; low inclusion is cited as a reason K-12 teachers feel less welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership facilitation of professional interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which MER leaders (co-directors, Advisory Committee) provide opportunities for professional interaction among mathematicians and mathematics educators and target workshops to attract a cross-section of groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate program design choices (targeting, leadership decisions) and whether leadership actively fosters cross-group workshops; lack of such facilitation is noted as a missed opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for and use of published education research
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition by MER participants of published education research and the expertise of mathematics educators, fostering mutual respect and better cross-community collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether MER presentations incorporate and respect findings from education research; the report argues that recognizing expertise in other fields helps build bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique niche / reaching mathematicians not involved elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: MER’s ability to duplicate some services of math-education organizations but uniquely reach research mathematicians who do not participate in those other organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a metric of organizational niche and strategic value: even if duplicative, reaching a different audience is valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual-level change indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Common individual changes attributed to MER: (1) enhanced awareness of educational issues, (2) strengthened feelings of support, (3) improved classroom pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are treated as primary individual outcomes; survey proportions and open-ended responses support attribution (e.g., ~60% reported association helpful to their projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom pedagogy changes (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific pedagogical changes reported by mathematicians following MER involvement, including cooperative learning, incorporation of technology (graphing calculators, DERIVE, Mathematica), more hands-on activities, increased class participation, reformed curricula (e.g., Harvard Calculus), and new assessment types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as evidence for pedagogical impact; many respondents attributed changes to MER workshops, publications, and networking. Examples include insisting students explain/justify computations, take-home exams with partner collaboration, student presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive atmosphere / reduced isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: MER’s role in creating a supportive atmosphere for educational reform activities, reducing feelings of isolation and increasing willingness to contact colleagues about professional matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured via survey items about comfort contacting MER colleagues and subsequent contact frequencies by topic (personal teaching, reform issues, mathematical research). High comfort/contact rates indicate successful networking/support functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental attitude change indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad changes at departmental level: improved attitudes toward education reform, increased acceptance/support, new projects/programs supported by departments, and more positive departmental atmosphere over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items ask whether involvement in reform is highly valued, whether atmosphere is one of acceptance/support, and whether the atmosphere has become more positive; use percent agreement and supporting quotations to assess influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary indicators of positive departmental change
rubrics_metrics.description: Three primary indicators: (1) improvements in curricula, (2) new institutional support, and (3) attention to better pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete curricular changes (e.g., calculus reform), institutional supports (seminars, grants, administrative backing), and pedagogical initiatives as evidence of departmental-level reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of faculty involved in educational activities (by activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Department-level metric reporting percent of faculty involved in: K-12 math education reform; undergraduate math-ed reform; teacher preparation; reform of graduate education for mathematics students; reform of graduate education for math-education students; teacher in-service activities; and mathematics research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 14 provides distribution categories (0%, 1-20%, 21-40%, etc.); use these to assess departmental engagement breadth and intensity. The report highlights that educational activity involvement is generally much lower than mathematics research involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustaining reform requires institutional reward changes / workload considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: For educational reform to be sustained in departments, the reward structure and institutional expectations must support faculty participation; respondents report long work hours and the need to balance research and reform activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional policies (tenure/promotion criteria, workload allocation) and reported time distribution; lack of institutional support is a barrier to sustained department-level reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (Jenness & Barley definition — development/reform of systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform is characterized by development of new or reformulation of existing systems rather than simply conducting new programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to judge whether changes are structural (system change) versus programmatic (isolated projects). The report adopts this definition to evaluate MER’s influence on systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (engagement of key partners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform involves the engagement of key partners in effective relationships to promote change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether MER fosters partnerships across stakeholders (math departments, education departments, K-12, administrators) and whether those relationships are effective and sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (identification of new roles/relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform includes the identification of new roles and relationships for all players inside and outside the educational system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether MER activities lead to redefined roles (e.g., teachers in policy roles, mathematicians engaging in reform leadership) and new collaborative arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (building infrastructure vs project mentality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic change is about building infrastructure for reform rather than the 'project mentality' of adding new programs; it replaces/revises system elements rather than simply adding new ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for structural investments and institutionalization of reform efforts rather than short-term projects; look for evidence MER contributed to infrastructure (departmental programs, seminar series, curricula embedded in department).

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (focus on internal change and strengths)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform focuses change on oneself first rather than on others and builds on system strengths rather than fixing deficits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether MER encourages reflective, internally-driven changes and leverages existing strengths in institutions instead of only diagnosing deficits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (long-term, multi-dimensional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform is a long-term, evolving process that addresses all dimensions of the system rather than focusing on one or two elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longitudinal indicators and multiple dimensions (curriculum, pedagogy, policy, roles, resources) to judge systemic influence; short-term or single-dimension changes are insufficient evidence of systemic reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (building capacities and marshaling resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform requires building capacities and marshaling resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for capacity-building activities (professional development, infrastructure) and evidence that MER aided in mobilizing financial/human resources for sustained reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (mainstreaming and lessons learned vs replication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform involves being part of mainstream reform efforts and focusing on lessons learned rather than concentrating on creating models for replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether MER-connected initiatives are integrated into mainstream institutional practice and whether the emphasis is on learning and adaptation, not solely on packaging 'replicable' models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systemic reform criteria (placing power in system actors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic reform places power in the hands of those in the system rather than relying only on funders or top-down change agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether MER supports decentralization of decision-making and empowers local actors (teachers, departmental faculty) in reform processes.
